summary: BifrOSt covers a Linux AT-SPI2 screen-reader bridge (roles, states, text attributes, text events, announcements, element notifications as signals, secure fields, named custom actions, pressable shell chrome) and system accessibility settings that apps read in one struct (display options, text size, Display Zoom, running assistive technologies, and opening a feature's Settings page). Screen reader earcons, Speak Selection, Speak Items Under the Pointer, a Braille line and app-requested audio graphs are wired in the shell. The kit's sidebar, toolbar, sheets, menus, segmented controls, path bar, player and mini month publish their hierarchy; apps that draw without the kit stay flat. Braille output has no device driver yet.

features.note: Apps receive reduce_motion and text_scale through Configure; contrast and transparency reach apps through the renderer (calendar-desktop follows them, see springboard/apps/calendar-desktop/CHANGELOG.md). No single SDK AccessibilitySettings struct. The accessibility_display service now returns increase contrast, reduce transparency, differentiate without colour, invert colours, reduce motion and dim flashing lights, and pushes options_changed on any change. Needs a Midget check. The shell itself honours Reduce Motion (desk.rs, mod.rs, switcher and jiggle through anim_ms), Reduce Transparency (vibrancy.rs, glass.rs, control_center.rs, desktop_bar.rs, quicksearch.rs) and Increase Contrast (ui.rs separators and material borders, appearance.rs colour contrast). Checked by reading the code, not on Midget. Built 2026-10-24 (parity/accessibility, host tests only): one SDK struct, sdk::accessibility_settings::Settings, read with one `settings` call and followed by `settings_changed`: display options, show borders, animated images (off with Reduce Motion), bold text, text scale, Display Zoom, Live Captions, application_accessibility and the running technologies (screen reader, switch control, voice control, screen zoom, keyboard navigation). open_feature/feature_supported open Dwell Control or AssistiveTouch in Settings (raw values of the reference settings-feature enum kept: 1..6). Still false because BifrOSt has no setting: non-blinking caret, reduce highlighting effects, horizontal text layout, action-slider alternative, Assistive Access. Tests: sdk accessibility_settings::tests, shell services::accessibility_display::tests. features.feature: Audio graphs and hearing device support
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 9 tests. Wave 2 (theme-31, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No audio graph or hearing aid API found in this pass. Built 2026-10-17: shell::audio_graph turns the chart tones into notes (a rest keeps its timing) and SoundPlayer::audio_graph plays the render on the sound-effects role; tests shell::audio_graph::tests and media::system_sound::tests::an_audio_graph_plays_through_the_stream_and_an_empty_one_writes_nothing. No SDK call or shell path asks for a graph yet. Built 2026-10-24 (parity/accessibility, host tests only): apps request a graph with sdk::audio_graph::play(ctx, chart, series); the audio_graph service checks the tones (512 tones, 1..2000 ms, 0 or 20..8000 Hz, a minute in all), accepts only the app in front and queues one graph; the binary renders and plays it (AudioJob::Graph). Hearing devices: no paired-device or streaming-ear API (no MFi hearing devices on Linux).

gaps: Apps that draw without the kit helpers (and the shell's built-in windows) still publish flat lists or nothing.
The search field in the shell chrome has no live text on the AT-SPI bus.
The AT-SPI bridge is untested on a live Orca; unit tests cover wire round trips, mapping and the action index.
Spoken Content: Speak Items Under the Pointer speaks app elements only (not the menu bar, dock or built-in windows) and its delay is fixed.
Custom actions: exported and runnable, but no app declares any yet.

Accessibility settings: non-blinking caret, reduced highlighting, horizontal text layout, the action-slider alternative and Assistive Access have no BifrOSt setting and always read false; Personal Voice, call audio, pointer devices and caption styles have no Settings page to open.
Braille: the reader's line is kept ready as cells, but no Braille display driver exists, so nothing reaches a device.
Hearing devices: no paired hearing-device or streaming-ear API.
